dialogue:
[doctor] hi , {PATIENT_FIRST} . it's good to see you . how have you been since your last visit in the spring ?
[patient] hi , doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} . better than last year , i think . my husband came along , he likes to check on the medicines .
[patient] somebody has to . she forgets her evening pill when the house is busy .
[doctor] that's always the hard part . how many episodes of the racing heartbeat have you had since we last talked ?
[patient] three that i noticed . the last one was about two weeks ago , in the middle of a shift . my heart went from normal to racing in a minute and a half , and i had to sit down on the floor of the hallway .
[doctor] tell me about the shift . what do you do for work ?
[patient] i'm a respiratory therapist at {ORG} , mostly nights in the emergency department . it's intense , and i was doing three codes that week . i think the adrenaline has something to do with it .
[doctor] that's very plausible . how long did the episode last ?
[patient] maybe forty minutes before it settled on its own . i checked my watch the whole time . the watch recorded the strip , and i sent the printout to the portal .
[doctor] yes , i saw it . it's an irregular rhythm at about one hundred and sixty with no clear p waves , which fits atrial fibrillation .
[patient] i was scared because my mom had a stroke at fifty-six .
[doctor] that's important family history . let's talk about the blood thinner . are you taking the apixaban twice a day ?
[patient] the eliquis , yes , five milligrams in the morning and at night . i have n't missed one in the last month . my husband sets up the pill box every sunday .
[doctor] good . any bleeding , bruising , or blood in the urine ?
[patient] i bruise easily on my shins from the bed frame , but that's been the same for years . no blood in the urine .
[doctor] okay . and the metoprolol ?
[patient] fifty milligrams twice a day . i get tired on it , especially in the afternoons , and my hands are cold when i'm on my feet all shift .
[doctor] that's a known side effect . how about your heart rate at rest ?
[patient] usually sixty something when i'm not at work . i rode my bike here today , actually , it was only four miles .
[doctor] wonderful . i'm glad you're getting exercise . what kind of exercise do you do ?
[patient] i swim at five forty five every morning at the rec pool , and on weekends i restore vintage motorcycles in my garage . my husband thinks it's a fire hazard .
[patient] it's a fire hazard . we have a fire extinguisher right next to the workbench .
[doctor] okay , and how old are the kids now ?
[patient] they're about four months . we just adopted them in the spring . it's been a whirlwind .
[doctor] congratulations . that's a lot for anyone , especially with your schedule . how are you sleeping ?
[patient] poorly , honestly . i wake up every two hours for the babies , and sometimes the monitor triggers the palpitations , or maybe it's the caffeine .
[doctor] the sleep disruption is certainly a trigger . let's cut back on caffeine after noon and keep the evening routine steady .
[patient] i'll try . the pot of coffee at work is the problem .
[doctor] i understand . let me listen to your heart . your rhythm is regular today , at seventy two . there's a soft click in the middle of the chest and a small late systolic murmur , which fits the mitral valve prolapse we saw on the echo .
[patient] is that serious ?
[doctor] it's common and usually mild . the echo showed only mild regurgitation , and your left ventricle is a normal size with normal pumping function .
[patient] okay . that's a relief .
[doctor] your blood pressure today is one eighteen over seventy four . your lungs are clear , and there's no swelling in your ankles .
[patient] good .
[doctor] your cholesterol panel from last month looks good , with an ldl of ninety six . your a one c is normal .
[patient] i was worried about my weight . i'm at one forty , and my husband says i should be at one thirty .
[doctor] a healthy weight is a reasonable goal to work on . the most important thing right now is the rhythm and the stroke prevention . our target for your blood pressure is under one thirty , based on the washington guidelines .
[patient] right . what about the ablation ? my coworker had one and she said it was life changing .
[doctor] that's an option for people with frequent symptomatic episodes despite medicine . we can refer you to our electrophysiologist for a discussion . given how infrequent your episodes are , i'd like to see the monitoring data first .
[patient] the monitoring is the patch thing ?
[doctor] yes . i'd like to order a seven day patch monitor to capture how often the rhythm happens during normal life and during your shifts . we'll decide about the ablation after that .
[patient] the patch won't get wet in the pool , right ?
[doctor] it's water resistant , but i'd ask you to skip the pool while it's on . take it off for showers .
[patient] okay . i'll tell the other nurses too .
[doctor] also , keep a symptom diary with the time , the activity , and how long each episode lasts . bring it to the next visit .
[patient] i'm good at lists . my husband will help with the times .
[doctor] perfect . if you get chest pain , fainting , or a racing heartbeat that doesn't settle within an hour , go to the emergency room . don't drive yourself .
[patient] i understand . thank you .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and mitral valve prolapse on anticoagulation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old female who presents for cardiology follow-up accompanied by her husband, who assists with medication management. She reports three episodes of palpitations since her last visit. The most recent occurred about two weeks ago during an intense night shift, with abrupt onset of rapid heartbeat and lightheadedness requiring her to sit down. The episode lasted approximately 40 minutes and resolved spontaneously. A wearable device recorded an irregular rhythm around 160 bpm without clear P waves, consistent with atrial fibrillation.

She works as a respiratory therapist at {ORG}, primarily in the emergency department on nights. She notes that stressful shifts and adrenaline may precipitate episodes. Her mother had a stroke at age 56.

She reports intermittent sleep disruption since adopting twin infants this spring, with waking every two hours, and wonders whether caffeine intake from work coffee contributes to palpitations. She swims at 5:45 each morning and restores vintage motorcycles in her garage on weekends. She cycled to clinic today.

She denies syncope or chest pain. She reports easy bruising on the shins from contact with the bed frame; she denies hematuria or melena.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Nonrheumatic mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation on echocardiogram. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed this year.

MEDICATIONS

Apixaban 5 mg by mouth twice daily. Metoprolol tartrate 50 mg twice daily, with fatigue in the afternoons and cold extremities. Caffeine, as above.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 118/74, heart rate 72 and regular at the time of exam. Cardiac exam: midsystolic click with late systolic murmur at the apex. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema.

RESULTS

ECG today: sinus rhythm. Transthoracic echocardiogram from prior evaluation: mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation, normal left ventricular size and systolic function. Lipid panel: LDL 96 mg/dL. Hemoglobin A1c within normal limits. Weight 140 lb.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with symptomatic episodes, triggered by stress, sleep disruption, and caffeine. Continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily; adherence reviewed. Continue metoprolol. Seven-day patch monitor ordered to quantify burden. Electrophysiology referral if episodes remain frequent; catheter ablation discussed as an option.
2. Nonrheumatic mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation; surveillance echocardiogram per schedule.
3. Hypertension prevention: blood pressure target under 130/80 per the Washington guidelines; current 118/74 is at goal.
4. Lifestyle: limit caffeine after noon, maintain sleep routine, weight reduction goal discussed. Symptom diary to be kept with times, activity, and episode duration.
5. Return precautions reviewed: chest pain, syncope, or sustained palpitations lasting over one hour warrant emergency evaluation.
